welcome.tagline:
Your keys, your coins.
Simple as a tap.
welcome.featureNoMnemonicBody: Create and sign in with a passkey on your device — no 12 words to copy down and guard.
welcome.featureOneAddressBody: The same address works on every supported network, and you can add your own.
welcome.featureOpenSourceBody: The app and backend services are open source — you can run a stack that is entirely your own.
welcome.featureKeyCustodyTitle: Keys live in your password manager
welcome.featureKeyCustodyBody: Passkeys are kept by Apple Passwords or Google Password Manager — Vela never touches them.
welcome.featureSafeContractBody: Accounts are built on audited Safe contracts, not a custom implementation.
welcome.featureStablecoinGasBody: Most networks let you pay fees in stablecoins — no need to hold the native coin first.
welcome.heroSubtitle: Sign with a passkey. Vela never sees your key.

intro.noSeedBody: Create your wallet with this device's fingerprint or face. No twelve words to write on paper, hide in a drawer, and fail to find one day.
intro.custodyBody: Your passkeys live where you keep them: this device's password manager, or a hardware security key. Vela can't reach them, and can't spend for you.
intro.chainsBody: The same address works on 12+ networks, and fees can be paid in stablecoins — no stocking up on a native coin for each one.

meta.title: Vela Wallet — the passkey wallet
meta.description: A passkey wallet with no seed phrase: one address across 12+ networks, audited Safe v1.4.1 contracts, stablecoin gas, fully open source and self-hostable.

create.alertNotDiscoverableBody:
Your device saved this passkey only on this device, so it wouldn't appear when you sign in and couldn't recover your wallet later. To keep you safe, no wallet was created — nothing is lost.

In system settings, set Google Password Manager or iCloud Keychain as your passkey provider, then simply try again.

That is a permissions setting rather than a fault in the key — on Linux, install your distribution's FIDO udev rules (libu2f-udev, or systemd 252 and later, which sets them up itself), then unplug the key and plug it in again.

funding.title: One quick step before you send
funding.lead: Your transactions run on a small {{symbol}} fee reserve. Add it once below — later transactions top it back up.
funding.statusConfirming: Your network fee is on its way — usually under a minute.
funding.networkHint: Withdrawing from an exchange? Choose the {{network}} network.
funding.qrHint: Scanning fills in the amount and network automatically
funding.detailsBody: It goes into a dedicated network-fee reserve that Vela maintains for you — one per network. It fronts the on-chain cost of your transactions and is replenished from each transaction's fee. It can only be spent on network fees and can't be withdrawn.
funding.denialDefault: The free top-up didn't go through this time. Add it below, or try again later.
funding.denialNotRecognized: Brand-new wallets can take a few minutes to be recognized — we'll retry the free top-up automatically. Or add it below to send right now.
funding.denialNonceExceeded: The free top-up covers a wallet's first few transactions, and this wallet is past that. Add it below to continue.
funding.denialTreasuryDepleted: Vela's free allowance is temporarily used up. Add it below, or check back later.
funding.denialBalanceTooLow: The free top-up needs your wallet to already hold some {{symbol}}. Receive some first, or add it below from any wallet or exchange.
funding.denialRateLimited: You were topped up just moments ago. If it's still short, add the difference below.
funding.denialTransferFailed: The free top-up transfer failed. Retry, or add it below.
funding.denialServiceUnavailable: The free top-up service is having a moment — we'll retry automatically. Or add it below.
funding.denialNetworkError: Couldn't reach Vela — check your connection. We'll retry automatically.
funding.denialPendingUnknown: Couldn't confirm the last top-up — watching your balance now. If nothing arrives shortly, add it below.
